bola-ahmed-tinubu.name: Bola Ahmed Tinubu
bola-ahmed-tinubu.summary: Nigerian politician serving as the 16th president of Nigeria since 2023. He previously served as governor of Lagos State from 1999 to 2007 and as senator for Lagos West in the Third Republic.
biography: Tinubu rose to national prominence as a leading figure in the progressive opposition that later formed the All Progressives Congress (APC).
As Lagos governor he oversaw reforms in revenue collection, urban planning and transport. In 2023 he won the presidential election on the APC ticket with Kashim Shettima as running mate.

history.title: Governor of Lagos State
history.detail: Two-term governor; known for fiscal and urban reforms.

history.title: APC formation
history.detail: Key architect of the merger that created the All Progressives Congress.

history.title: Elected President
history.detail: Defeated Atiku Abubakar (PDP) and Peter Obi (LP) in the February 2023 election.

atiku-abubakar.name: Atiku Abubakar
atiku-abubakar.summary: Nigerian politician and businessman who served as vice president from 1999 to 2007 under President Olusegun Obasanjo. He has contested the presidency multiple times, including as PDP flag bearer in 2019 and 2023.
biography: Atiku began his career in the Nigeria Customs Service before entering politics and business. He was elected governor of Adamawa in 1999 but became Obasanjo's running mate before inauguration.
He remains one of Nigeria's most persistent presidential aspirants, finishing runner-up in both 2019 and 2023.

history.title: Vice President
history.detail: Served two terms with President Olusegun Obasanjo.

history.title: Presidential campaigns
history.detail: Multiple bids across parties; PDP nominee in 2019 and 2023.

history.title: PDP presidential nominee
history.detail: Finished second nationally with Ifeanyi Okowa as running mate.

peter-obi.name: Peter Obi
peter-obi.summary: Nigerian politician and businessman who served as governor of Anambra State. He was the Labour Party presidential candidate in 2023 and finished third nationally.
biography: Obi built a reputation for frugal public finance as Anambra governor. In 2022 he left the PDP and emerged as Labour Party's presidential candidate, galvanising a large youth and diaspora following.
His 2023 campaign with Yusuf Datti Baba-Ahmed reshaped Nigeria's three-way presidential contest.

history.title: Governor of Anambra
history.detail: Completed interrupted terms after court and impeachment battles.

history.title: LP presidential candidate
history.detail: Third place nationally with about 25% of the vote.

rabiu-kwankwaso.name: Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso
rabiu-kwankwaso.summary: Influential Kano politician and leader of the Kwankwasiyya movement. He contested the 2023 presidency on the NNPP platform and finished fourth.
biography: Kwankwaso has been a dominant figure in Kano politics for more than two decades, alternating between PDP and APC before leading NNPP's national ticket in 2023.

history.title: Governor of Kano (1st term)
history.detail: First democratic tenure after the military era.

history.title: Governor of Kano (2nd term)
history.detail: Returned via PDP before later joining APC, then NNPP.

omoyele-sowore.name: Omoyele Sowore
omoyele-sowore.summary: Journalist, activist and founder of Sahara Reporters. He founded the African Action Congress and contested the presidency in 2019 and 2023.
biography: Sowore is known for citizen reporting and pro-democracy activism. He launched AAC in 2018 and has remained a vocal critic of successive Nigerian governments.

history.title: Presidential candidate
history.detail: AAC flag bearer in two general elections.

muhammadu-buhari.name: Muhammadu Buhari
muhammadu-buhari.summary: Nigerian general and politician who served as military head of state (1983-1985) and as civilian president from 2015 to 2023.
biography: After decades of opposition politics, Buhari won the 2015 election as APC candidate, becoming the first opposition candidate to defeat an incumbent Nigerian president, and was re-elected in 2019.

history.title: Military Head of State
history.detail: Came to power after a coup; later overthrown.

history.title: Left office
history.detail: Handed over to Bola Tinubu after completing two civilian terms.

goodluck-jonathan.name: Goodluck Jonathan
goodluck-jonathan.summary: Nigerian politician who served as president from 2010 to 2015. He was the first sitting president to concede defeat after losing re-election.
biography: Jonathan rose from Bayelsa deputy governor to vice president, then president after Umaru Yar'Adua's death. He lost the 2015 election to Muhammadu Buhari.

history.title: President
history.detail: Completed Yar'Adua's term and won the 2011 election.

history.title: Lost re-election
history.detail: Conceded to Buhari - a landmark peaceful transfer.

hamza-al-mustapha.name: Hamza Al-Mustapha
roles: Former Chief Security Officer to Gen. Sani Abacha
hamza-al-mustapha.summary: Retired Nigerian Army major and intelligence officer who served as Chief Security Officer to Head of State Gen. Sani Abacha. He was the Action Alliance presidential candidate in 2023.
biography: Al-Mustapha was a central figure in Abacha's security apparatus. After years in detention and subsequent release, he entered partisan politics and contested the 2023 presidency.

history.title: AA presidential candidate
history.detail: Contested on the Action Alliance ticket.

adewole-adebayo.name: Adewole Adebayo
adewole-adebayo.summary: Nigerian lawyer, activist and media entrepreneur. He was the Social Democratic Party presidential candidate in 2023.
biography: Adebayo is known for public commentary on law and governance and for founding KAFTAN TV. He ran for president on the SDP platform in 2023.

kola-abiola.name: Kola Abiola
kola-abiola.summary: Businessman and son of the late Chief MKO Abiola. He was the Peoples Redemption Party presidential candidate in 2023.
biography: Kola Abiola entered the 2023 race on the PRP ticket, invoking the democratic legacy associated with his father's June 12 mandate.

christopher-imumolen.name: Christopher Imumolen
christopher-imumolen.summary: Accord Party presidential candidate in the 2023 general election, cleared on INEC's final national list.
biography: Imumolen contested the 2023 presidency as the Accord (A) flag bearer.

dumebi-kachikwu.name: Dumebi Kachikwu
dumebi-kachikwu.summary: African Democratic Congress presidential candidate on INEC's 2023 final list.
biography: Kachikwu was listed by INEC as ADC's presidential candidate for the February 2023 election.

yabagi-sani.name: Yabagi Sani Yusuf
yabagi-sani.summary: Action Democratic Party presidential candidate for the 2023 election.
biography: Sani contested as ADP flag bearer in the February 2023 presidential election.

peter-umeadi.name: Peter Umeadi
peter-umeadi.summary: Former Chief Judge of Anambra State and APGA presidential candidate in 2023.
biography: Umeadi was APGA's presidential nominee on INEC's final 2023 list.

chichi-ojei.name: Princess Chichi Ojei
chichi-ojei.summary: Allied Peoples Movement presidential candidate in 2023 - one of the few women on the national ballot.
biography: Ojei contested the presidency on the APM ticket in February 2023.

osita-nnadi.name: Osita Nnadi
osita-nnadi.summary: Action Peoples Party presidential candidate for the 2023 election.
biography: Nnadi was APP's presidential candidate on INEC's final national list.

sunday-adenuga.name: Sunday Oluwafemi Adenuga
sunday-adenuga.summary: Boot Party presidential candidate in the 2023 general election.
biography: Adenuga contested as Boot Party flag bearer in February 2023.

felix-osakwe.name: Felix Johnson Osakwe
felix-osakwe.summary: National Rescue Movement presidential candidate for 2023.
biography: Osakwe was NRM's presidential candidate on INEC's final list.

ado-ibrahim.name: Abdulmalik Ado-Ibrahim
ado-ibrahim.summary: Young Progressives Party presidential candidate in 2023.
biography: Ado-Ibrahim contested the presidency on the YPP ticket.

daniel-nwanyanwu.name: Daniel Daberechukwu Nwanyanwu
daniel-nwanyanwu.summary: Zenith Labour Party presidential candidate for the 2023 election.
biography: Nwanyanwu was ZLP's presidential candidate on INEC's final national list.

obadiah-mailafia.name: Obadiah Mailafia
obadiah-mailafia.summary: Economist and former Central Bank of Nigeria deputy governor. He was ADC's presidential candidate in 2019.
biography: Mailafia contested the 2019 presidency on the ADC platform.

donald-duke.name: Donald Duke
donald-duke.summary: Former Cross River State governor and 2019 Social Democratic Party presidential candidate.
biography: Duke governed Cross River for two terms and later sought the presidency on the SDP ticket in 2019.
